scenario: Taxi driver with sixteen days of low back pain after lifting, radiating to the left leg; penicillin allergy.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Good morning Suresh. Please sit. How are you?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Good morning doctor. I am okay, just this back pain. Fuel prices have gone up again, so I cannot even rest at home, I have to keep driving.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Where exactly is the pain?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Lower back, on the left side mostly, and it goes down the back of my left leg, till the knee.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: When did it start? Was there any injury?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: About two weeks ago. I lifted a gas cylinder up the stairs and felt something pull. Two weeks, no, sixteen days, I counted.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any numbness in the legs, weakness, or any problem passing urine or stool?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No numbness. No weakness. And urine and stool are normal, no problem there.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Good. Have you had back problems earlier?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes, in 2019 they said slip disc, I took rest for one month. After that, fine.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: What are you using for the pain now?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Volini spray on the back, and paracetamol, two or three tablets a day. Not much help.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any medicine allergy?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I am allergic to penicillin. My face swelled up, years ago.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Noted, thank you. Let me examine you. Bend forward please. There is tenderness over the lower left back muscles. When I lift your left leg, it is painful at about forty degrees. The right leg is fine. Reflexes are normal.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, I drive a taxi, ten hours a day. Will this affect my job? I cannot sit out for a long time.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: You have a muscle strain in the lower back. And maybe some irritation of a nerve from the old disc problem. I do not think it is serious right now.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Do I need any tests?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Not today. If it is not better after ten days, we will do an x-ray of the lower back, and possibly an MRI.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: And tablets?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Aceclofenac 100 milligrams twice a day after food for five days, and pantoprazole 40 milligrams before breakfast to protect your stomach. Continue paracetamol if needed.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. Can I go to work?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: You can drive, but stop every hour and walk for five minutes. Do not lift anything heavy for three weeks. Use a hot water bag at night. A physiotherapist will teach you some back exercises.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Understood. And when do I come again?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Review after ten days, and earlier if you get numbness, weakness, or trouble passing urine.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Thank you doctor.

gold.key: goes down the back of my left leg
tenderness over the lower left back muscles
stop every hour and walk for five minutes

notes: Fuel-price remark in turn 1 is small talk (the chief complaint in the same turn is labelled). The self-correction in turn 5 (two weeks, then sixteen days) resolves to sixteen days. Turn 7 denies the back-pain red flags (numbness, weakness, bladder or bowel change) as negated symptoms. In turn 18 the x-ray and MRI are conditional on no improvement but are still investigation mentions. The follow-up condition in turn 18 (not better after ten days) is not labelled separately. Turn 24 also lists return-early triggers that are not labelled as red_flag (hypothetical advice). The patient takes volini and paracetamol; the doctor adds aceclofenac and pantoprazole and continues paracetamol. Drug names such as aceclofenac and pantoprazole are hard for a speech synthesiser and recogniser.
